response.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(derived_product_cost) AS avg_cost, SUM(derived_total_cost) * 1.0 / SUM(product_price) AS ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), overall AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM inv), kept AS (SELECT i.avg_cost, i.ratio FROM inv i CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE i.ratio > o.avg_ratio) SELECT AVG(k.avg_cost) AS avg_line_product_cost, AVG(k.ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(k.ratio - o.avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio_excess FROM kept k CROSS JOIN overall o;

assumptions.assumption: Each invoice's ratio is SUM(derived_total_cost) / SUM(product_price), with each column's NULLs skipped independently. An invoice whose price sum is zero or NULL gets a NULL ratio, so it is left out of the overall average and the filter.
Each invoice counts once in the averages, and the average line product cost per invoice ignores NULL derived_product_cost values.
'How far their ratio exceeds the overall average ratio' is the plain difference (kept ratio minus overall average ratio), not a percentage.

alternatives.interpretation: The ratio uses only lines where both derived_total_cost and product_price are present, so the numerator and denominator cover the same set of lines.
alternatives.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(derived_product_cost) AS avg_cost, SUM(CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND product_price IS NOT NULL THEN derived_total_cost END) * 1.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND product_price IS NOT NULL THEN product_price END) AS ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), overall AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM inv), kept AS (SELECT i.avg_cost, i.ratio FROM inv i CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE i.ratio > o.avg_ratio) SELECT AVG(k.avg_cost) AS avg_line_product_cost, AVG(k.ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(k.ratio - o.avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio_excess FROM kept k CROSS JOIN overall o;
